name: Broccoli (sprouting)
grown_as: Purple sprouting broccoli, picked as many small spears. William's records list 'Early Purple Sprouting' (sown in spring, overwinters, picked February to April) and 'Summer Purple' (picked the same year). White sprouting kinds exist.
habit: A tall, sturdy plant 60 to 100 cm on a thick stem, with large leaves. Instead of one head it makes many small loose heads (spears) 5 to 10 cm long at the top and from every leaf joint.

leaf.type: Simple, often with a few small lobes on the lower part of the blade
leaf.outline: Long and oblong to obovate, 30 to 50 cm, with small lobes near the base
leaf.base: Narrowing into a long stalk, the small lobes running down it
leaf.margin: Wavy and irregularly scalloped, no sharp teeth
leaf.veins: A thick pale midrib (often purple-tinged) and strong side veins
leaf.surface: Hairless, with a waxy grey bloom
leaf.stalk: Long and thick, often flushed purple
leaf.colour: Blue-green, often tinged purple, especially in cold weather

flower.form: A cross-shaped flower of four petals
flower.petals: Four, free, broad and rounded with a long narrow claw, spreading flat
flower.centre: Six stamens, four long and two short, with yellow anthers, round a green style
flower.behind: Four narrow upright green sepals hugging the petal claws
flower.carried: In long, loose spikes on a tall branched stem; the closed buds stay above the open flowers at the top of each spike

fruit: Long, slender pods 5 to 10 cm, cylindrical with slight bumps over the seeds, ending in a short beak 0.5 to 1 cm, spreading upwards along the stems. Green, drying straw-brown and splitting from the bottom to show a pale papery partition. Seeds round, 2 mm, dark red-brown to grey-black.
seedling: Two kidney-shaped seed leaves on short stalks, broader than long with a notch at the tip, like a heart with the stalk at its point, waxy grey-green; the first true leaves oval to round on long stalks, waxy blue-green with wavy edges.
winter: Early kinds stand through winter as tall leafy plants, the spears forming from late winter.

leaf: a long blade with wavy edges and small lobes near the base
a long thick stalk, often purple-tinged
bloom: four pale yellow rounded petals in a cross
narrow upright sepals hugging the claws
closed buds above the open flowers
seed: round dark red-brown to grey-black seed 2 mm
seedling: two kidney-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip
young: an upright plant of long-stalked waxy blue-green leaves
crop: many small loose spears of purple buds on green stalks
spears at the top and from the leaf joints, each with small leaves
a tall plant with large blue-green leaves
flower: the spears opened out into branching stems
seedhead: long slender pods with short beaks along tall stems

look_alikes: Calabrese makes one big green head. Kale flowers in spring with small yellow-green shoots but its leaves are frilled or deeply cut. All the cabbage-family crops (cabbage, cauliflower, broccoli, sprouts, kale) are one species and share the waxy blue-green leaf; they differ in what is eaten. Swede and oilseed rape have bluish clasping stem leaves but their young leaves are hairy. Turnip and pak choi (Brassica rapa) have bright yellow flowers held above their buds.
